reference_sql:
WITH export_days AS (
  -- one row per Dublin day: purchase events, 1 to 7 December 2025
  SELECT event_date AS day, COUNT(*) AS export_purchases
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
    AND event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
  GROUP BY event_date
), first_paid AS (
  -- one row per subscription: when its first payment came in, refunded or not
  SELECT subscription_id, MIN(paid_at) AS first_paid_at
  FROM payments
  GROUP BY subscription_id
), backend_days AS (
  -- one row per Dublin day: the subscriptions whose first payment fell on it
  SELECT strftime(timezone('Europe/Dublin', first_paid_at), '%Y%m%d') AS day, COUNT(*) AS backend_first_payments
  FROM first_paid
  WHERE strftime(timezone('Europe/Dublin', first_paid_at), '%Y%m%d') BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
  GROUP BY day
)
SELECT e.day, e.export_purchases, b.backend_first_payments,
  e.export_purchases - b.backend_first_payments AS difference
FROM export_days e
JOIN backend_days b ON b.day = e.day

WITH both_sides AS (
  -- one row per purchase event or first payment, with its Dublin day and its side
  SELECT event_date AS day, 'export' AS side
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
    AND event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT strftime(timezone('Europe/Dublin', first_paid_at), '%Y%m%d'), 'backend'
  FROM (/* one row per subscription: its first payment */ SELECT subscription_id, MIN(paid_at) AS first_paid_at FROM payments GROUP BY subscription_id) AS f
  WHERE strftime(timezone('Europe/Dublin', first_paid_at), '%Y%m%d') BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
)
SELECT day,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE side = 'export') AS export_purchases,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE side = 'backend') AS backend_first_payments,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE side = 'export') - COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE side = 'backend') AS difference
FROM both_sides
GROUP BY day

WITH export_days AS (
  -- one row per Dublin day: purchase events, 1 to 7 December 2025
  SELECT event_date AS day, COUNT(*) AS export_purchases
  FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase'
    AND event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
  GROUP BY event_date
), first_paid AS (
  -- one row per subscription: when its first payment came in, refunded or not
  SELECT p.subscription_id, p.paid_at AS first_paid_at
  FROM payments p
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments q WHERE q.subscription_id = p.subscription_id AND q.paid_at < p.paid_at)
), backend_days AS (
  -- one row per Dublin day: the subscriptions whose first payment fell on it
  SELECT strftime(timezone('Europe/Dublin', first_paid_at), '%Y%m%d') AS day, COUNT(*) AS backend_first_payments
  FROM first_paid
  WHERE strftime(timezone('Europe/Dublin', first_paid_at), '%Y%m%d') BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
  GROUP BY day
)
SELECT e.day, e.export_purchases, b.backend_first_payments,
  e.export_purchases - b.backend_first_payments AS difference
FROM export_days e
JOIN backend_days b ON b.day = e.day

  WHERE strftime(timezone('Europe/Dublin', first_paid_at), '%Y%m%d') BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
)
SELECT day,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE side = 'export') AS export_purchases,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE side = 'backend') AS backend_first_payments,

other_way.tradeoff: Stacking both sides with UNION ALL keeps a day that only one side has, but one step then holds two kinds of rows.

solver.query:
WITH e AS (
  SELECT event_date AS day, COUNT(*) AS c FROM events
  WHERE event_name = 'purchase' AND event_date BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
  GROUP BY event_date
), b AS (
  SELECT strftime(timezone('Europe/Dublin', first_paid_at), '%Y%m%d') AS day, COUNT(*) AS c FROM (SELECT subscription_id, MIN(paid_at) AS first_paid_at, arg_min(amount_eur, paid_at) AS first_amount FROM payments GROUP BY subscription_id) f
  WHERE strftime(timezone('Europe/Dublin', first_paid_at), '%Y%m%d') BETWEEN '20251201' AND '20251207'
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT e.day, e.c AS export_purchases, COALESCE(b.c, 0) AS backend_first_payments,
  e.c - COALESCE(b.c, 0) AS difference
FROM e LEFT JOIN b ON b.day = e.day
